frozen_config.target: p(U, rho, beta, omega, lambda_rep, lambda_back | x, S*, z*, epsilon) proportional to p_RFS(x | S*, z*, h(U), scalars, epsilon) p(U|rho) p(rho) p(beta) p(omega) p(lambda_rep) p(lambda_back)

likelihood_branch.name: utility-weighted frontier
likelihood_branch.feasibility: F(x) = prod_{z precedes x} q(z), empty product 1
likelihood_branch.utility: Q(x) = log(1 + S(x)),  S(x) = sum_z 1[x precedes z] (1 - q(z))
likelihood_branch.back_cost: C_back(x) = sigmoid(omega) * sum_{z != x} 1[x precedes z] q(z)
likelihood_branch.state_update: q(y)=1; q(x) *= (1 - sigmoid(omega)) for x downstream of y
likelihood_branch.not: uniform-frontier (beta would not multiply a utility term)

boundaries.segmentation: none — boundaries are known and fixed
boundaries.blocks: every block is one independent trace of fixed length T
boundaries.q_reset: q_0 = 0 at the start of every block; q never crosses a block boundary

numerics.exponent_stabilisation: row-wise max subtraction before exp; cancels in the normalisation

structural_model.latent: U in R^{m x d} continuous latent utility matrix
structural_model.induced_order: h(U): i > j iff U[i,r] > U[j,r] for every r; the intersection of the d column orderings
structural_model.legality: every real U induces a legal strict partial order; no acyclicity check exists or is needed
structural_model.mcmc_state: U itself (continuous); the poset is a derived label
structural_model.prior: rows iid Normal(0, Sigma_rho), Sigma_rho = (1-rho) I_d + rho 11^T
structural_model.rho_is: correlation between the d latent COLUMNS within a row; rows are iid. Not a row covariance -- that would need a matrix-normal prior
structural_model.rho_dependent_normaliser: -(m/2) log|Sigma_rho|, present in log_u_prior; cancels in a U update at fixed rho, does NOT cancel in a rho update at fixed U
structural_model.combinatorial_normaliser_reason: the prior is a density on R^{m x d}, not a score over a set of partial orders, so no sum over legal posets arises

dimensions.note: m, d and K are three different integers; the brief writes the latent column count as K, the repository writes it as d and reserves K for the skill count

spec_divergences.brief_assumes: U^(0)/U^(a) assessor hierarchy with a tau dependence
spec_divergences.frozen_reality: a single U in R^{5x2}; no assessor level, no tau
spec_divergences.resolution: use the frozen state, as the brief's own fallback clause directs; the assessor-residual density and the hierarchical QMC construction have no referent and are not built

spec_divergences.frozen_reality: rho ~ Beta(1, 1) truncated at 1 - 5e-3, i.e. Uniform(0, 0.995), from StatisticalUtils.dRprior with stage5.RHO_PRIOR = 1.0
spec_divergences.resolution: the brief defers to the final Stage 6C configuration, which establishes this prior

spec_divergences.brief_assumes: rho scaling proposal delta ~ U(d_r, 1/d_r) with ratio -log(delta)
spec_divergences.resolution: sections 6 and 7.2 require reusing the frozen Stage 6C rho update and proving numerical equality with it; adopting the scaling proposal would fail that gate. The scaling proposal's density ratio is implemented and tested as a non-production utility so the identity is still pinned

model.sizing_rationale: dimensions chosen for reference quality before any MCMC comparison existed: 30 blocks x T=8 gave relative ESS 0.005 with a max weight of 0.10, which section 10.2 forbids accepting; 3 blocks x T=5 gives relative ESS 0.081 and leaves the induced-H posterior genuinely uncertain

transforms.rho: exact prior inverse CDF: Beta(1,1) truncated at 0.995 renormalised == Uniform(0, 0.995)
transforms.U: non-centred: U = Z L(rho)^T with L L^T = Sigma_rho

qmc.weight: w = p_RFS(x | state); the proposal IS the joint prior, so no prior density remains in the weight

gate_rationale.max_rqmc_standard_error: rqmc_se = sd(replicate_estimates, ddof=1)/sqrt(R) is the uncertainty of the quantity the comparison consumes, the replicate mean. Independent scrambles make the per-replicate estimates iid, which licenses the formula.
gate_rationale.max_structural_half_width_95: t(0.975, R-1) * rqmc_se. At 2.5e-3 the reference's own 95% uncertainty occupies at most 25% of the 0.01 total-variation and relation-marginal error budget it feeds, leaving the remaining 75% to detect a genuine sampler defect.
gate_rationale.max_replicate_h_total_variation: Retained as a DIAGNOSTIC of replicate exchangeability, not as a precision measure. Set at 3e-3, which is what a per-replicate dispersion can plausibly reach at this ESS; it is deliberately not derived from the observed 1.7e-3.
gate_rationale.max_replicate_relation_departure: As above, for the relation marginals.

superseded_gates.why_mis_specified: The maximum absolute departure across R independent scrambles estimates the dispersion of a SINGLE replicate. It is not an estimator of the uncertainty of the averaged reference, which is what the downstream comparison actually uses, and it has no reason to decrease as R or N grow — the maximum of a fixed number of draws from a tightening distribution shrinks only as fast as that distribution, and the max over 8 values is itself a high-variance statistic. Observation bore this out: doubling N from 2^18 to 2^19 left the maximum essentially unchanged (1.704e-3 -> 1.727e-3) while the log-evidence standard deviation fell as expected. The gate was therefore measuring the wrong quantity, not detecting an inadequate reference.

provenance: The original max-replicate-spread gate (1e-3) failed at 2^18 and 2^19 BEFORE any Stage 6D1 production MCMC comparison was run.
The corrected gate is derived from estimator uncertainty (rqmc_se and its 95% half-width) and from the downstream 0.01 error budget.
No MCMC result was inspected, computed or used to select the new thresholds; the Stage 6D1 production comparison had not been run when they were registered.

The observed 0.0017 replicate spread was NOT adopted as the new threshold; the secondary dispersion gate is 3e-3, chosen from what a per-replicate dispersion can reach at this ESS rather than from the observation.
reference_registration.fallback_rule: If the primary precision gates fail, increase R from 8 to 32 — more independent scrambles reduce sd/sqrt(R), the standard error of the averaged reference. Do NOT expect, or wait for, the maximum replicate range to shrink; that statistic is not what the gate measures. Invoke the section 10.2 mixture-importance fallback only if ESS, maximum weight, replicate dispersion or the revised precision gates remain inadequate after the R = 32 run. Never select whichever replicate agrees best with MCMC.

precision.definition: rqmc_se = sd(replicate_estimates, ddof=1)/sqrt(R); the half-width is t(0.975, R-1) * rqmc_se

reference_quality.fallback_rule: If the primary precision gates fail, increase R from 8 to 32 — more independent scrambles reduce sd/sqrt(R), the standard error of the averaged reference. secondary_gate_addendum.observation: max_replicate_h_total_variation rose from 0.001796 at R=8 to 0.003529 at R=32 and now exceeds its 3e-3 threshold, while every primary precision gate improved by the predicted factor of sqrt(4).
secondary_gate_addendum.diagnosis: The secondary dispersion gate is ITSELF a maximum over replicates and therefore inherits the same defect that retired the original 1e-3 gate. Taking a maximum over 32 draws instead of 8 samples further into the tail, so the statistic grows with R even though the reference is strictly more precise. Its 3e-3 threshold was implicitly tied to R=8 and is not comparable across R.
secondary_gate_addendum.action_taken: None. The threshold has NOT been raised to accommodate the observation, and the diagnostic is reported as FAILED. It is labelled a diagnostic of replicate exchangeability rather than a precision measure in the registration, and the decision to proceed rests on the primary precision gates, which pass.
secondary_gate_addendum.why_this_is_not_evidence_of_a_worse_refe: The quantity the comparison consumes is the replicate MEAN. Its uncertainty is rqmc_se = 0.000791 with a 95% half-width of 0.000533 on structural probabilities, i.e. about 5% of the 0.01 downstream budget. Per-replicate dispersion is a property of N, which did not change.
secondary_gate_addendum.recommended_correction_for_a_future_stag: Replace the max-over-replicates dispersion diagnostic with an R-invariant one, e.g. the pooled per-replicate standard deviation, or a max compared against an explicitly R-dependent expected-maximum reference.

reference_quality.frozen_note: Reference frozen at R=32, N=2^19 after the primary precision gates passed. No Stage 6D1 production MCMC comparison had been run at the time of freezing.

attempts.label: attempt 2 — omega x32, 50,000 sweeps
attempts.reconstruction: **Re-execution, not the original chain.** The omega-retuned attempt's directory was overwritten by the third attempt's rerun, and its base seed was never written down. Re-running the recorded configuration (omega x32 = 5.82816, the other three scalars at their registered values, 50,000 sweeps) at each seed that appears anywhere in the Stage 6D1 record — [6020000, 0] — reproduces the attempt's *finding* but not its exact numbers, so no seed can be claimed as the original. These artifacts are the configuration re-run at base seed 0; the numbers recorded at the time are listed beside them and are what the report cites as the attempt's own result. Nothing here is presented as the original chain.

continuation_history.status: Stage 6D1 sampler correctness: PASS. All eleven registered gates pass simultaneously at the initial 50,000 sweeps; no continuation was needed and the 100,000 ceiling was not approached.

attempt_history.outcome: FAIL - beta 1.01184 and lambda_rep 1.01457 at 50k; extended to the ceiling, which fixed both but pushed omega to 1.01205
FAIL - omega fixed decisively (1.01205 -> 1.00006, bulk ESS 650 -> 45,433) but beta failed at 1.03094 (50k) and 1.01334 (ceiling)

efficiency_gain.reading: All four scalars were 16-32x under-scaled. The registered Stage 6B scales were tuned on the 500-block corpus, where the posterior is far tighter than on this deliberately small 3-block reference model.

registration.purpose: choose proposal scales for the Stage 6D2 formal run on the frozen 500-block corpus, using efficiency information only
registration.why_stage6d1_scales_are_not_reused: the Stage 6D1 corrections (16-32x) were tuned on a 3-block T=5 reference model whose posterior is deliberately broad; the Stage 6D2 posterior is much tighter, so those multipliers are expected to be far too large. The registered Stage 6B scales are equally unverified here because they were tuned with U fixed at the truth and the other scalars held fixed.
registration.why_U_and_rho_are_in_scope: Stage 6D1 froze U and rho by explicit instruction. No such instruction covers Stage 6D2, and the corpus is ~167x larger, which changes the U acceptance regime directly: a U row move is scored against 500 blocks of likelihood rather than 3.
registration.selection_rule: largest median ESJD among admissible; ties to the smaller multiplier
registration.esjd_note: U uses squared Frobenius movement of the whole matrix over a sweep; rho uses squared movement of logit(rho); the log-scale scalars use squared movement of log(x). Raw-space ESJD on a log-scale kernel biases selection toward oversized scales.
registration.sequential_rule: each coordinate is frozen at its selection before the next is tuned; later coordinates keep their base scales until their turn

grid_extension_rule.direction: toward larger scales if every median acceptance exceeds the admissible band, toward smaller scales if every median acceptance falls below it

registration.starts: the registered Stage 6D2 formal starts, imported from scripts/stage6d_oracle_joint_mcmc.chain_start
forbidden_and_not_computed: R-hat or ESS from candidate pilot runs

stage6d1_scales_for_contrast.note: recorded for the report only; never used as a starting point here

joint_confirmation.note: confirmation only, not another optimisation round

relation_count.note: relation count is constant across all draws and chains; R-hat and ESS are undefined, not passing

uncertain_relations.note: a relation that never varies has no R-hat; averaging one in would flatter the report, so only the varying relations are scored

beta.note: reported contrast, not a gate: Stage 6C2 fixes omega, lambda_rep and lambda_back while Stage 6D2 marginalises over them, so the two beta marginals are not supposed to be equal. The Stage 6B3 row above is the like-for-like comparison.

parents_disagree_with_each_other.reading: the gap between the two parents is itself the size of the effect of conditioning on omega and the lambdas rather than marginalising over them; it is not a defect in either.

interpretation.U_beta: beta agreeing with Stage 6B3, which pinned U at the truth while marginalising over the same three other scalars, means marginalising over U does not move beta: no U-beta confounding.
interpretation.H_omega: the induced order agreeing with Stage 6C2's, where omega was fixed, means freeing omega does not move the structure: no H-omega confounding.
interpretation.rho_U: rho agreeing with Stage 6C2's means the extra three free scalars do not reach rho, which is expected because rho enters only p(U | rho) and the order posterior is unchanged.

rho.recovery: NOT APPLICABLE — no generating value exists
rho.why: U_TRUE is hand specified in recurrent_synthetic.py rather than drawn from p(U | rho); no RHO_TRUE exists and none may be manufactured by regenerating a more favourable dataset.

stage6d2_column_audit.note: a large signed-contrast R-hat with a small invariant-summary R-hat is label switching, not non-convergence; H and relation probabilities are the reported quantities and are invariant

entrywise_posterior_mean_U_is_not_a_vali.why: averaging U entrywise across the posterior collapses the incomparabilities: every draw realises the same partial order, but their mean lands in a region where all coordinates are strictly ordered, so h(mean U) is a denser order than h(U) for any draw. The likelihood reads U only through h(U), so this plug-in scores a different model. It is reported as a negative control — a concrete demonstration of why entrywise U recovery is not claimed — and not as a competitor.

stage6d2_heldout.note: secondary reporting only; not used to choose a proposal scale, a prior or a threshold. The prior-mean row is a floor, not a competitor.

relation_count_rhat.note: degenerate: the relation-count trace is constant at 6.0, which is the point mass Stage 6C established on this corpus. R-hat is undefined, not 1.0. The point mass itself is gated by structural recovery.

uncertain_relation_rhat.note: no relation varies across the retained draws, so there is no per-relation R-hat to compute; not applicable rather than passing on a vacuous 1.0

rho_matches_stage6c2.note: rho enters only p(U | rho), so conditional on the same order posterior it cannot depend on the scalars Stage 6C2 held fixed

structure_matches_stage6c2.note: freeing omega, lambda_rep and lambda_back must not move the induced order

verdicts.Stage 6D rho recovery: NOT APPLICABLE — no generating value exists
verdicts.Stage 6D entrywise U recovery: NOT CLAIMED — the target is invariant

shortfalls: **No independent reference exists for the Stage 6D2 corpus, and none can be built by the Stage 6D1 route.** Prior importance sampling degrades as the likelihood sharpens; at 30 blocks of `T = 8` the relative ESS was already 0.005 with one point holding 10% of the weight. Stage 6D2's correctness claim is therefore *inherited* from Stage 6D1 and supported by parent consistency, not established afresh.

**`rho` remains weakly identified**, exactly as Stage 6C found. The order posterior is a point mass and `rho` never enters the likelihood, so `p(rho | Y)` is driven entirely by how one order's prior cell mass varies with `rho`, on five rows of a two-dimensional Gaussian.

**The Stage 6D1 pilot's `replay_per_sweep_ok` flag was off by one** — it compared against `sweeps x (m + 1)` and omitted the single replay that builds the initial state, so it recorded `false` on every row. The flag is reported, never read by the selection rule, so no scale was affected. The Stage 6D2 pilot compares against `1 + sweeps x (m + 1)` and records both the observed and the expected count.
**Unknown boundaries, skill-label inference and semi-Markov FFBS are not started.** Stage 6D is the last stage that runs on oracle segmentation and oracle labels.
